title: Notes above and below the staff
summary: Short extra lines carry the staff further up and down.

steps.title: Ledger line
steps.body:
Notes too high or too low for the five lines get short extra lines of their own, called **ledger lines**. Middle C sits on one ledger line just below the treble clef, and on one just above the bass clef: it is the note the two clefs share.

**Why it matters:** Middle C, and many melody notes, are written on ledger lines. Seeing middle C on one is your anchor between the two clefs.

steps.title: Above the treble clef
steps.body: A above the top line sits on one ledger line.

steps.title: Find the anchor
steps.body: Play middle C, then read upward on the treble clef (D, E, F) and downward on the bass clef (B, A, G).
